title: Hybrid proactive-reactive autoscaler: headroom validator and scale-commit ledger
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Implement a hybrid autoscaling policy engine that synthesizes proactive (predictive warmup + demand forecasts) and reactive (quantile-backed latency/throughput targets) signals into a validated scale decision, while enforcing safety limits via a scale-commit ledger. This ticket scopes the policy spec, validator checks, ledger semantics, and integration points with request routing (KV cache affinity) and dedicated fleet admission. Deliverable: an engine that outputs deterministic scale intents with safety guarantees and audit trail for committed capacity changes.
target_metrics: primary: sustained_tokens_per_sec (tenant-level) -> translated to node_count target
secondary: p99_inference_latency_ms (end-to-end) used to trigger reactive steps
gpu_utilization_pct as stability signal (avoid scaling oscillation during transient peaks)
queue_depth_requests and cold_kv_miss_rate as warmup triggers
scaling_algorithms: predictive-warmup: short-horizon forecast (30-90s) using EWMA of token/sec + diurnal baseline
quantile-backed reactive controller: target percentile (p90/p95) throughput-to-sla translator
bounded-stepper: step size capped by scale-commit ledger (max nodes / minute), slew-rate limits
derivative-damping: limit acel/decel when rate-of-change of demand exceeds threshold
lease-based commitments: ephemeral capacity leases to support immediate bursts with timed reconciliation
safety_limits_and_guards: min_headroom_tokens_per_sec = 15% of requested target unless overridden by tenant SLA
surge_budget_credits: banked credits consumed for short bursts (token-balanced accounting)
cooldown_window_seconds = 90s default before scale-down allowed after scale-up
kv-affinity-preservation: prefer scaling nodes that retain hot KV shards to avoid cache churn
circuit-breaker: automatic fallback to lower-cost model variant if commit ledger cannot satisfy request within Xs
proposed_solution: Add a new Policy Orchestrator component that (1) gathers signals from forecasting service, runtime telemetry (latency/queue/kvs), and tenant SLAs; (2) runs a validator that simulates applying candidate scale intents against safety limits and current commit ledger; (3) emits a preflight decision which is logged to the scale-commit ledger; (4) persists the ledger entry and issues an actionable scale command to the Fleet Controller. Ledger entries include reason, metric snapshot, predicted demand window, and lease expiration. The validator rejects intents that violate headroom, ramp rate, or breach per-tenant caps, producing human-readable failure reasons for ops and tiebacks to console alerts.
acceptance_criteria: 1) System produces deterministic scale intents for synthetic demand traces (unit/integration tests) and passes validator checks
2) Ledger stores a verifiable audit trail for each committed scale intent (reason, user/automated actor, pre/post metrics)
3) End-to-end tests: when synthetic warmup trace triggers predictive warmup, nodes are pre-provisioned before p95 latency breach in 90% of runs
4) Safety limits prevent >40% ramp for all stress tests and cooldown prevents oscillation for repeated bang-bang patterns
5) KV-affinity preference reduces cold_kv_miss_rate by >= 30% during controlled scale-ups compared to naive placement
6) Console surfaces ledger entries and validator rejections with links to relevant traces/PRs
tradeoffs: Conservative headroom increases cost for sustained low-latency SLAs but reduces dropped requests and rollbacks
Lease-based bursts improve perceived SLAs for tenants but complicate capacity accounting; requires clear billing/chargeback semantics
Strong KV-affinity heuristics reduce cache churn but may reduce packing efficiency and slightly increase steady-state cost
Predictive warmup reduces p99 tail but can introduce unnecessary scale-ups on noisy forecasts; mitigated by validator tolerance thresholds
testing_plan: Unit tests for validator rules and ledger mutation semantics
Integration tests with Fleet Controller stub to assert timing and ramp constraints under controlled traces
Chaos test that kills nodes during ramp to verify rollback and ledger reconciliation
Load tests using replayed production traces (dashboard: /dashboards/autoscale/hybrid-validator) to measure p99 and cost delta
A/B experiment on small dedicated cluster with 10 tenants comparing new policy vs current baseline for 2 weeks
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flag behind 'hybrid_autoscaler_v1' in staging for smoke tests
2) Canary rollout to 5% of dedicated fleets (non-enterprise tenants) for 72h with automated health gates
3) If canary stable, expand to 25% for 7 days with close monitoring of ledger rejects and cold_kv_miss_rate
4) Gradual ramp to 100% with ops playbook for manual rollback and ledger-driven audit if anomalies observed
5) Post-rollout retrospective and cost analysis scheduled in Cycle following full rollout
observability_and_metrics_to_add: scale_commit_latency_ms (time from intent -> ledger persisted -> fleet action)
per-tenant headroom_coverage_ratio (fraction of time headroom >= configured target)
